clue.text: Treacherous foe in bad — or in good — faith

indicators.note: a treacherous thing cannot be trusted to stay as it is, so the following words are rearranged

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone may act in bad faith or good faith toward a treacherous enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes split 'in good faith' around the clue's 'or', which sets the definition against the wordplay's 'bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase bona fide literally means 'in good faith', describing honest intentions without deceit.

clue.text: Cook is to be found in Scottish bank

indicators.note: something found in another thing sits inside it, so one piece is put within the other

blocks.note: a brae is a Scots word for a hillside or slope
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook is located at a bank in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bank' is a hillside, not a financial institution.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook food slowly in a little liquid in a covered pot, so it is a cooking verb.

clue.text: Compound of citrin, a kind of acid

definitions.note: adjective standing for the type of acid: nitric acid

indicators.note: a compound mixes ingredients together, so the next word's letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; citrin is a plant compound

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: citrin forms part of a certain type of acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitric acid is a strong mineral acid, so the word names one particular sort of acid.

clue.text: He purveys foodstuffs to two monarchs

blocks.note: apples, pears and so on are foodstuffs
ER (Elizabeth Regina) twice

explanation.surface: A royal supplier delivers groceries to a pair of kings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foodstuffs' does double duty: it is in the wordplay but also colours the definition. ER is the abbreviation for Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruiterer is a shopkeeper who sells fruit, so he is a man who purveys goods.

clue.text: Argument said to stir people in Bow?

blocks.note: first meaning: a quarrel
second, playful meaning: a quarrel is what gets people worked up, here in the East End

explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of London's East End. The second half is a loose, whimsical hint rather than precise wordplay: a row is what stirs people up.
explanation.definitionFit: A disagreement is a difference of opinion that turns into a dispute, which is exactly what an argument is.

clue.text: Goes without a partner to drink and chat

indicators.note: without means lacking something, so a letter is taken away from the first word

blocks.note: taken as written
in bridge, East is the partner of West
to sip is to drink in small amounts

explanation.surface: A lonely person attends unaccompanied, has a drink and natters.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit as North, South, East and West, so a partner is one of those compass letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is idle talk about other people, so it works as a verb meaning to chat.

clue.text: Duck cavity is egg-shaped

blocks.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, which looks like O
a void is an empty space

explanation.surface: A duck's hollow interior has the shape of an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a duck is a batter's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid comes from Latin ovum, egg, and describes an oval three-dimensional egg-like form.

clue.text: Start to smoke, crumble and burn without a flame

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: first letter of the word
to moulder is to decay and crumble away

explanation.surface: A fire that begins smoking, collapses and glows without flames.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to burn slowly with smoke but no visible flame, a precise dictionary match.

clue.text: Opening remarks before a walk?

blocks.note: the prefix meaning before
an amble is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: A speaker says a few words before heading out on a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamble is an introductory statement at the start of a speech or document.

clue.text: Selfless concern for others is a Liberal axiom

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal
a truism is a self-evident truth, like an axiom

explanation.surface: Caring for others is a basic principle of liberal thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is the principle of acting for others' wellbeing without regard to oneself.

clue.text: Playful because boy's around

indicators.note: the boy is around, that is surrounding, the preceding word

blocks.note: a common boy's name
colloquial short form of because

explanation.surface: Someone is in a jolly mood since their son is home.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means given to joking, humorous or jesting, so it is close to playful.

clue.text: Horse race set in the Lake District, say

blocks.note: the Grand National is the famous steeplechase, often just called the National
to park something is to put or set it down

explanation.surface: A horse race is staged in Cumbria's lake country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's best-known steeplechase at Aintree. 'say' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake District is one of England's protected scenic areas, an example of this kind of conservation landscape.

clue.text: Fast bird

blocks.note: first meaning: quick
second meaning: a fast-flying aerial bird

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase describing a quick bird, but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for speed and the name of a sickle-winged bird that feeds on the wing.

clue.text: Chief has to denounce contract

blocks.note: grand can mean main or principal
to slam is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A boss must publicly condemn an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a contract is the bid a side undertakes to make; bidding all thirteen tricks is the top one.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand slam is a bridge bid to win every trick, which is a contract in that game.

clue.text: Polluted area isn't fit to be a source of water

indicators.note: polluted things are spoiled and disturbed, so the next words' letters are scrambled

blocks.note: letters taken as written
well can mean healthy, fit

explanation.surface: A contaminated area cannot safely supply drinking water.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well taps groundwater under pressure that rises without pumping, so it is a water source.

clue.text: Infamous 1946 Hitchcock film

blocks.note: first meaning: well known for something bad
second meaning: the spy thriller starring Cary Grant and Ingrid Bergman

explanation.walkthrough: The first word seems to describe the film, but it is a definition in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone famous for wrongdoing, and it is also the title of Hitchcock's 1946 thriller.

clue.text: One ultimately hated being a "personality"

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
last letter of the word
an entity is a being, a thing that exists

explanation.surface: Someone eventually loathed being a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Personality and identity both mean the distinctive character that makes a person who they are.

clue.text: Intimidating, oddly pushy Chinese girl

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third and fifth letters are kept

blocks.note: letters 1, 3 and 5
abbreviation for Chinese
G is a standard abbreviation for girl

explanation.surface: An aggressive young woman from China is frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimidating' looks like it describes the girl, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Psyching someone out means unnerving them to gain an advantage, which is a form of intimidating.

clue.text: I train medics to be flexible and give different treatment

indicators.note: something flexible bends into other shapes, so the preceding words take a new arrangement

blocks.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher tells doctors to adapt their care to each patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To discriminate is to treat people or things unequally, making a distinction between them.

clue.text: Mafia scoundrels planted bomb

indicators.note: something planted is buried inside, so the answer lies concealed within the next words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Gangsters set an explosive device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bomb' is used in its informal sense of a flop, not an explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a complete failure, and to bomb or a bomb informally means a flop.

clue.text: Nurse co-ordinates heads of medical experiments to find a chemical catalyst

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, so the first of each is kept

blocks.note: an Enrolled Nurse
z and y are axes on a graph
first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A nurse arranges trial leads to identify a reaction-speeding chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is the old British title Enrolled Nurse. Co-ordinates here are the letters naming axes.
explanation.definitionFit: Enzymes are proteins that speed up biochemical reactions, acting as natural catalysts.

clue.text: Tory runs around with workers and sailors nearly all night

definitions.note: noun used attributively, as in 'night creatures'

indicators.note: running around means turning back the way one came, so the word is read backwards
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: short for Conservative
trade union
Royal Navy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Conservative campaigns all night among workers and sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all night' tempts as the definition, but 'all' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal means happening at night or active by night, so it serves as the adjective night.

clue.text: Complicated clue really beginning to make one sore!

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
complicated means tangled, so the letters are knotted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A solver groans that a tricky clue is giving them a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sore' reads as an adjective (upset), but it is a noun: a painful spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open sore on the skin or a mucous membrane.

clue.text: Some are ignoring government

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the answer is a run of letters inside it

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A few people are disregarding the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a period of rule, so it means the government of a monarch.

clue.text: A princess's artfully coy, provoking foolish behaviour

indicators.note: doing something artfully means arranging it cleverly, so the next word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a, meaning one, is the Roman numeral I
Princess Diana, widely known as Di
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal's calculated shyness brings out silliness in others.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocy is extremely stupid conduct, so it matches foolish behaviour as a synonym.

clue.text: Well, there's nothing dull about "The Apprentice"!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the dull word is wrapped round the learner

blocks.note: FA as in 'sweet FA', slang for nothing at all
mousy means drab and dull
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A TV viewer insists the business reality show is never boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet FA' is British slang for nothing at all. In Britain, a learner driver displays an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Famously can mean excellently, as in 'got on famously', so it is an informal synonym for well.

clue.text: Food stuff provides nothing good in Mongolian tent

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the following word

blocks.note: a yurt is the round felt tent of Central Asian nomads
zero, shaped like O
standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Supplies in a nomad's tent hold nothing worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: YURT is split around the other letters: YU before them, RT after.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is a fermented milk product eaten as food, a basic example of foodstuff.

clue.text: Slovakia is bound to have a piste

blocks.note: the international country code for Slovakia
taken as written
to lope is to move with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: Slovakia is certain to offer a ski run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain to', but it is a verb of movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a prepared run of compacted snow for skiing, i.e. a downhill course.
